name: Japan
targetIntake: September or October 2027 — Japan's autumn intake (May 2027 IB session)
tagline: A named minority route, on a calendar built for it
summary: Japan has a small, deliberate set of fully English-taught bachelor's degrees, and the IB Diploma is one of the qualifications they were built to receive. The University of Tokyo's PEAK has closed; its new English-taught College of Design opens in September 2027 and names the IB first. Around it sit Waseda's six English-based schools, Keio's PEARL, Sophia, ICU, Kyoto's iUP, Tohoku's new Gateway College, APU and Akita. The Japanese year starts in April, so the September and October intakes exist mainly for international applicants — which is why they fit a May 2027 IB session, and why every deadline falls between October 2026 and April 2027, before results.
whyConsider: The University of Tokyo opens a new English-taught faculty in September 2027 — its first new undergraduate faculty in about seventy years — with 50 of its 100 places on a route built for international qualifications and the IB named first.

Keio's PEARL runs three application periods for September 2027, the last closing on 7 April 2027, and accepts predicted IB grades in as many words. It is the latest Japanese deadline on this page and the one that fits a Danish school year.

Waseda's application window for September entry ran 8 January to 10 February in the most recent cycle — one application covering six English-based schools, late enough that predicted grades are settled.

Kyoto's iUP takes you with no Japanese at all: a six-month preparatory course, then four years of undergraduate study, 4.5 years in total, with fee waivers and monthly scholarships for eligible students.
National-university tuition in Japan is low by global standards, and private universities are far cheaper than their US or UK equivalents — though the 2027 figures are not confirmed here.

Money at the point of admission rather than by separate application: Waseda states that its scholarship recipients are determined by the admission result with no separate form, and Kyoto's iUP attaches fee waivers and monthly scholarships to eligible students. This matters more here than MEXT does, because the MEXT undergraduate scholarship is not offered to Danish nationals and depends, for everyone else, on the Japanese embassy in their country of citizenship — see the watch-outs.
Several programmes — ICU, Akita International University, APU — are built entirely around a bilingual liberal-arts model that maps naturally onto the IB's breadth.

The University of Tokyo opens its first new undergraduate faculty in about seventy years in September 2027, taught entirely in English, with half its hundred places on a route built for international qualifications and the IB named first.

Keio's PEARL runs three application periods for September 2027 entry, the last closing on 7 April 2027 and deciding on 24 May — the latest Japanese deadline on this page, and the only decision here that lands after the examination session.
Waseda takes one application for six English-based schools in a single winter window, which is unusually friendly against Japan's older October deadlines.

Kyoto's iUP asks for no Japanese at all: six months of intensive preparatory language teaching, then four years of undergraduate study, with admission and tuition fee waivers and monthly scholarships.

Money often comes with the offer rather than by separate application: Waseda decides its scholarships from the admission result, APU awards tuition reductions at admission, and Kyoto's iUP offers fee waivers and monthly scholarships.
Several programmes, ICU and Akita and APU among them, are built on a bilingual liberal-arts model that maps onto the Diploma's breadth.
watchOuts: The University of Tokyo's PEAK has ended — its own site states that September 2026 was the final student recruitment — but Todai has not closed to English-speaking school-leavers. The UTokyo College of Design opens in September 2027 and its applications close on 5 November 2026, the earliest Japanese deadline on this page. It is a five-year integrated bachelor's and master's programme, not a bachelor's degree.
UTokyo's other English route, the Global Science Course, is a third-year transfer programme requiring at least two years of undergraduate study outside Japan. It is not an entry point from gymnasium.

Tohoku's Future Global Leadership courses and Sophia's Green Science and Green Engineering courses took their last students in 2026. Tohoku replaces FGL with Gateway College (English-taught, October 2027 intake, applications 15 December 2026 to 14 January 2027); Sophia opens an English-taught Bachelor of Engineering in Digital Green Technology.

Deadlines are a major trap, and they are spread over six months with nothing joining them up: UTokyo College of Design closes 5 November 2026, Kyoto iUP 3 December, Kyushu 11 December, Tohoku Gateway College 14 January 2027, Keio PEARL in three periods between December 2026 and 7 April 2027, Waseda at a date not yet announced. Build the list in the autumn of 2026.

Two intakes means two calendars, and neither is September by default. The Japanese academic year runs April to March; April 2027 entry would mean applying in mid-2026 and is not realistic. Kyoto's iUP enrols in October, which is a third calendar again.

MEXT is not what it looks like from Europe. The undergraduate scholarship funds a year of preparatory Japanese followed by a degree taught in Japanese; English-medium study happens only through 'direct placement', which MEXT decides, and MEXT chooses your university with no objection allowed.

Which embassy handles MEXT depends on your nationality: MEXT tells applicants to ask "the Japanese Embassy or Consulate General in your country". If you hold Danish citizenship, the undergraduate scholarship is not open to you. The Embassy of Japan in Denmark's Study in Japan page (dated 3 December 2020) lists two MEXT types for Danish nationals, Japanese Studies and Research Student, both for students already at university. Its 2026 news list carries a single MEXT call, for Research Students 2027. For any other nationality, ask the Japanese embassy in that country whether it runs the undergraduate track. Either way, plan Japan's finances around institutional awards and JASSO, and get the embassy's answer in writing before you build a year around MEXT.

The only official tuition figure quoted here is the University of Tokyo's own, and it carries no price year. The fee table linked from Japan's official study-promotion site is drawn from the Student Guide to Japan 2019–2020 and is out of date by several years.

If you can claim Danish SU, it does not follow you to Japan on the same terms as to an EU/EEA country. Check with su.dk early; a full degree outside the EU/EEA has separate rules. If you cannot claim it, check whether your own country's student finance covers a degree outside Europe.
Japanese universities generally want documents apostilled and sometimes notarised, and a Certificate of Eligibility must be obtained before the student visa. Start three months before travel.

PEAK has ended, and that is not the same as Todai closing. The College of Design's applications for September 2027 close on 5 November 2026, the earliest deadline among these Japanese options, and it is a five-year integrated bachelor's and master's programme rather than a bachelor's degree.

Tohoku's FGL courses and Sophia's Green Science and Green Engineering courses took their last students in 2026. Tohoku's replacement, Gateway College, takes applications for October 2027 from 15 December 2026 to 14 January 2027.

April is the default intake and September is the exception. April 2027 entry would have meant applying in the middle of 2026 and is not realistic for this cohort; Kyoto's iUP enrols in October, which is a third calendar again.
There is no central portal, no shared calendar and no common application. Six months separate the earliest deadline from the latest, and each application carries its own fee.

MEXT is not a route into the English-taught sector. The undergraduate scholarship funds a preparatory year in Japanese followed by a degree taught in Japanese; English-medium study happens only through 'direct placement', which MEXT decides, and MEXT also chooses the university, with no objection allowed.

The MEXT undergraduate scholarship depends on your nationality: you apply through the Japanese embassy in your country of citizenship, and the embassy in Copenhagen does not offer it to Danish nationals. The Embassy of Japan in Copenhagen lists two MEXT types for Danish nationals — Japanese Studies and Research Student, both for students already at university. If you hold another nationality, check whether the Japanese embassy in that country offers the undergraduate type; otherwise plan around institutional awards, and ask the embassy in writing if MEXT matters to you.

The only official fee figure quoted here is the University of Tokyo's, and its page carries no price year. The fee table linked from Japan's official study-promotion site is drawn from the Student Guide to Japan 2019–2020.

Japanese universities generally want documents apostilled and sometimes notarised, and a Certificate of Eligibility must be obtained before the student visa. Neither fits inside a November deadline arranged in October.

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: There is no national rule. Each English-taught programme treats the full IB Diploma as meeting the twelve-year schooling condition and sets its own standard on top. The UTokyo College of Design is the one that publishes a number: it expects 38 of 42 points across the six subjects plus at least 2 for TOK and the Extended Essay, and says expectations 'are not cut off scores'. Keio's PEARL and Tohoku's Gateway College accept an IB Diploma or predicted grades.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: No national conversion table. Each university reads IB points directly.
notes: The IB Diploma is one of the qualifications Japan's English-taught programmes were explicitly designed to receive, alongside A-levels, the US high school diploma plus SAT/ACT, and the Abitur.

Predicted grades do the work. Every September or October 2027 decision on this page is made before 6 July 2027. Keio and Tohoku accept predictions in so many words; the UTokyo College of Design accepts a certified predicted score from anyone whose exams fall after its deadline, makes the offer conditional, and wants final results by 16 August 2027.

MEXT's scholarship route applies its own academic condition — twelve years of schooling completed by March of the arrival year, or by August where the applicant enters in the autumn term through direct placement. An IB Diploma completed in May sits between the two. For Danish nationals this is a secondary question, because the Embassy of Japan in Denmark does not offer them the undergraduate scholarship; for other nationalities it depends on the Japanese embassy in that country.
Some programmes also want SAT/ACT or a national university entrance examination for international students (EJU). Check each one — the requirements are not uniform.
The UTokyo College of Design expects 38/42 plus 2 core points, and says this is not a cut-off. No other programme on this page publishes a minimum.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Limited but real: a few dozen fully English-taught bachelor's programmes nationally, concentrated at Waseda (six schools), Keio, Sophia, ICU, Kyoto, Tohoku, Kyushu, Nagoya, Tsukuba, Hokkaido, APU and Akita. The UTokyo College of Design opens in September 2027; PEAK, Tohoku's FGL and Sophia's Green Science and Engineering courses have closed. No national total is given here.
language.englishProof: Set per programme, usually as a test. The UTokyo College of Design and Tohoku's Gateway College both want TOEFL iBT 80, IELTS 6.0, Duolingo 110 or Cambridge 169 or more; Keio PEARL wants TOEFL iBT or IELTS Academic. Whether an IB English A or B result replaces the test is not confirmed at any of them, so ask.
notes: Kyoto iUP explicitly states that Japanese proficiency is not required at the outset — the six-month preparatory course exists to build it.
No English-taught programme requires Japanese to enrol, but essentially all of them require you to study it, and you will need it for part-time work, housing and daily life.
APU and ICU are formally bilingual: you take courses in both languages as your Japanese improves.

feeContext.summary: Japan charges the same tuition to every nationality, so there is no EU/non-EU split to look for. The structure is a one-off admission fee plus annual tuition, with private universities well above national ones and science and engineering above the humanities. Budget for the admission fee separately: it is charged once and it is substantial.
feeContext.typicalRange: The University of Tokyo publishes an admission fee of 282,000 yen once and tuition of 642,960 yen a year — above the 535,800 yen national standard, which is why a national figure should never be quoted for a particular university. It is the only official institutional figure quoted here.
feeContext.priceYear: Not stated on the source page, read 2026-09-23

sources.title: The University of Tokyo charges an admission fee of 282,000 yen once and annual undergraduate tuition of 642,960 yen, the same for every nationality. The page states no academic year and says nothing about the College of Design.

The fee table still linked from Japan's official study-promotion site is drawn from the Student Guide to Japan 2019–2020 and converts at 114 yen to the dollar. It should not be used for a 2027 or 2028 budget.

livingContext.housing: Most English-taught programmes guarantee or strongly prioritise a first-year place in a university dormitory or international house, which is cheaper and far simpler than the private market. APU houses all first-year international students in AP House. Private renting in Japan involves key money, guarantor requirements and agency fees that are difficult to navigate from abroad — take the dormitory.
livingContext.healthcare: Enrolment in National Health Insurance is compulsory for anyone staying more than three months and is arranged at the municipal office when you register. It covers roughly 70 per cent of medical costs and students typically add the university's own supplementary cover. An EHIC does not apply.
livingContext.workRights: Students with College Student (留学) status may work up to 28 hours a week once they hold a blanket Permission to Engage in Activity Other Than That Permitted (Immigration Services Agency). Check the rules for longer hours in the official long vacations with your university.
livingContext.residency: EU citizenship changes nothing. The university applies for a Certificate of Eligibility once you accept an offer; you take it to the Embassy of Japan in Copenhagen for a Student visa. On arrival you receive a residence card, register at the municipal office within 14 days and enrol in National Health Insurance. Allow three months and expect documents to need an apostille.
funding: MEXT Undergraduate Scholarship, Embassy Recommendation: in the 2027 round, five years including a preparatory year in Japanese, 117,000 yen (about €650 at the ECB rate of 24 September 2026) a month, fees waived and air tickets paid, with MEXT choosing the university. The Embassy of Japan in Denmark does not offer this type to Danish nationals, so it is listed only because people ask about it.
University-recommendation MEXT places, under which a Japanese university nominates its own admitted students. The route exists; ask each admissions office whether it holds MEXT quota places.
JASSO Honors Scholarship, a monthly grant for privately financed international students. Check the current amount with JASSO.

Institutional awards decided at admission. Waseda states that its scholarship recipients are determined by the admission result with no separate application and that its awards are grants rather than loans; APU operates tuition-reduction scholarships at several levels; Kyoto's iUP offers admission and tuition fee waivers plus monthly scholarships.

funding.note: A full degree outside the EU/EEA follows separate rules, with its own ties-to-Denmark form: check su.dk before budgeting.

sources.title: The MEXT undergraduate scholarship on the Embassy Recommendation runs for five years from April 2027 to March 2032, beginning with one year of preparatory education in Japanese. It pays 117,000 yen a month, waives entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees and provides an economy air ticket. Applicants must be born on or after 2 April 2002 and have completed twelve years of schooling by March 2027, and in principle must arrive in Japan between 1 and 7 April 2027.

MEXT recruits embassy-recommended undergraduate scholars between April and May of the year before arrival, with first screening by the embassy or consulate between May and August; each country's exact schedule is set by its Japanese diplomatic mission.

The Embassy of Japan in Denmark offers Danish nationals two MEXT scholarship types, Japanese Studies and Research Student, and both are for students already at university. The undergraduate scholarship is not among them.
A student with College Student (留学) status can hold blanket permission to work part-time up to 28 hours a week.

sectorLandscape.summary: Japan's official answer to what its higher education is made of names five kinds of institution international students may enter, and English-language guidance almost always stops at the first. Beyond the 大学 sit 短期大学 junior colleges, 高等専門学校 kōsen that take students at fifteen for a five-year technical programme, 専門学校 professional training colleges, and since 2019 the 専門職大学 professional and vocational universities. The English-taught undergraduate sector is not one of these categories: it is a named set of programmes inside the first one, on a September or October intake that the rest of the system does not use.

routes.what: Four years to a bachelor's degree, six for medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine and pharmacy. National, local public and private, and the difference is largely money — the private universities charge considerably more and hold most of the English-taught provision. Every programme on this page sits here.
routes.note: The English-taught programmes inside this category are a named minority, admitted through their own rounds, on their own calendar, often at a different time of year from the Japanese-medium cohort at the same university.

routes.what: Two or three years ending in an associate degree rather than a bachelor's. Heavily weighted towards early-years and primary teaching, nursing and allied health, nutrition, home economics and design, and historically towards women students.
routes.note: MEXT names it as one of the five routes open to international students. Whether any junior college admits an IB holder in practice, and in what language, is not known.

routes.what: A five-year engineering and technology programme entered at fifteen, straight from lower secondary, with a two-year advanced course on top. Fifty-one national kōsen plus local public and private ones. Graduates are hired by Japanese manufacturers in numbers out of all proportion to the sector's size.
routes.note: It is rarely mentioned in English-language advice. An IB Diploma holder is four years too late for the ordinary entry point; the advanced course and third-year transfer could in theory apply, so ask a kōsen directly.

routes.what: Post-secondary specialised training: two-year diploma courses of 62 credits or more and four-year advanced diploma courses of 124 or more, in animation and game design, IT, hospitality and cookery, fashion, care work, automotive engineering and dozens of other named trades.
routes.note: It is a large part of Japanese post-secondary education by student numbers, it enrols many international students, and it is rarely mentioned in English-language guidance for IB students. Only MEXT's own description of it is covered here.

routes.what: Created in 2019 to sit between the university and the professional training college: four years to a bachelor's degree (professional), or two to three years to an associate degree (professional), with a substantial compulsory placement built into the curriculum.
routes.note: A recent category in the Japanese system, with little documentation in English.

routes.englishName: Japan campus of a foreign university
routes.what: A foreign university operating in Japan and awarding its own home degree. Temple University, Japan Campus teaches entirely in English in Tokyo and allows transfer to Philadelphia.
routes.note: Useful if you want an American-style degree with a Japanese life around it, and priced accordingly — it charges American tuition, not Japanese.

Japan admits international students to five kinds of higher education institution — colleges of technology, specialized training colleges on post-secondary courses, junior colleges, universities and graduate schools. Most institutions run an academic year from April to March and admit in April, though some operate an autumn admission system.

The University of Tokyo opens a new English-taught undergraduate faculty, the UTokyo College of Design, in September 2027. It takes 100 students on a five-year integrated bachelor's and master's programme through two routes, and Route B is for applicants using international qualifications, the International Baccalaureate Diploma named first among them. Applications run from 15 October 2026 at 09:00 to 5 November 2026 at 17:00 JST.
PEAK has stopped recruiting permanently. September 2026 was its final intake and no further applications will be accepted.

Tohoku's Gateway College, a new English-taught undergraduate programme, admits about 90 students for October 2027 entry with applications from 15 December 2026 to 14 January 2027 and results on 24 March 2027; it accepts the IB with predicted scores and wants IELTS 6.0, TOEFL iBT 80, Duolingo 110 or Cambridge 169. Tohoku's separate English page states that FGL undergraduate admissions ended in 2026.

Sophia's English-taught undergraduate degrees are the Faculty of Liberal Arts, the Sophia Program for Sustainable Futures and a Bachelor of Engineering in Digital Green Technology; Green Science and Green Engineering have closed to new applicants.

notes: Audited 2026-09-24. Dates were read for the University of Tokyo, Keio, Waseda, Kyoto, Kyushu and Tohoku; the other institutions are listed with their programmes but their rounds were not read.
Re-check in November 2026, when Waseda is expected to publish its September 2027 window, and again in April 2027 for the MEXT 2028 guidelines.

Not established: any minimum IB score other than the UTokyo College of Design's stated expectation; most application fees; the JASSO Honors Scholarship amount; living costs from an official page; and the university-recommendation route into MEXT.
The Embassy of Japan in Denmark's pages refuse plain fetches (HTTP 403) but open in an ordinary browser; the Study in Japan page was read that way on 2026-09-24.

portal.name: No central portal — apply direct to each university

deadlines.label: UTokyo College of Design, Route B, September 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: Opens 15 October 2026 at 09:00 JST. Route B is the international-qualifications route (50 of the 100 places) and lists the IB. A separate video assignment is due 13–16 November 2026, first screening result 22 December 2026, final decision 20 February 2027. With predicted grades the offer is conditional and final results are due by 16 August 2027.

The UTokyo College of Design's Route B expects an IB level of 38/42 in the six subjects plus 2 core points, not as a cut-off; applicants whose exams fall after the deadline submit certified predicted scores, receive a conditional offer, and must submit final results by 16 August 2027. Designated English tests: TOEFL iBT over 80, IELTS over 6.0, Duolingo over 110, Cambridge over 169.

deadlines.label: Keio PEARL, Period III, September 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: The last of three periods sharing about 100 places; Periods I and II close 2 December 2026 and 27 January 2027. Result 24 May 2027 — after the examination session, before results. Keio accepts predicted IB grades explicitly. Application fee JPY 35,000.

sources.title: Keio's PEARL economics degree admits about 100 students for entry on 22 September 2027 through three separate application periods, the last of which closes on 7 April 2027, and it accepts an IB Diploma or predicted IB grades.

deadlines.label: Waseda English-based undergraduate programmes, September 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: One application window covering the School of Political Science and Economics, School of Social Sciences, SILS, School of Culture Media and Society, and the two Science and Engineering schools. As of 23 September 2026 the only window published is 8 January to 10 February 2026, labelled for September 2026 entry. Check Waseda's page for the 2027 dates.

sources.title: Waseda offers English-based undergraduate degrees at six schools, four of them September-entry only and two taking April entrants as well. As of 23 September 2026 the only application period published is the one for September 2026 entry, 8 January to 10 February 2026; no dates for September 2027 entry had been posted.

deadlines.label: Kyoto University iUP, October 2027 enrolment
deadlines.notes: Applications open 2 November 2026. Kyoto's own Apply page gives the period as "November 2 until December 3, 2026 (5 p.m. Japan Standard Time)". Screening stages and result dates are in Kyoto's guidelines PDF.

sources.title: Applications to Kyoto's iUP for October 2027 enrolment run from 2 November to 3 December 2026, closing at 17:00 JST.

deadlines.label: Kyushu University international undergraduate programmes, October 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: A five-day window: the online application system is open only from 7 to 11 December 2026, so do not plan to start the form on the 11th. Kyushu then wants "all the necessary documents by post" as well. For the English-taught engineering programmes and Bioresource and Bioenvironment. No closing time is stated.

sources.title: Kyushu University's English-taught undergraduate programmes (engineering, and Bioresource and Bioenvironment) take online applications for October 2027 entry from 7 to 11 December 2026.

deadlines.notes: Application period 15 December 2026 to 14 January 2027; first-stage result 5 February, second stage 21–22 February, successful applicants announced 24 March 2027. Predicted IB scores are accepted. No closing time is stated.

PEAK's front page puts it in the past tense — "the applications for September 2026 enrollment are now closed", "this was the final student recruitment for PEAK, and no further applications will be accepted". Its successor is not a replacement PEAK but the UTokyo College of Design, which is listed above.

deadlines.notes: No undergraduate MEXT call appears on the Embassy of Japan in Denmark’s site: its news list for the whole of 2026 carries exactly one MEXT call, for Research Students, with an application deadline of 15 June 2026. MEXT’s national rule — recruitment in April and May of the year before arrival — therefore describes a window a Danish national cannot use through this embassy. If you hold another citizenship, the embassy track runs through the Embassy of Japan in your country of citizenship — check its own call for that window. Because this rests on what the embassy's site does not list, write to the embassy at info@ch.mofa.go.jp before relying on it either way. The route that plausibly remains open to a school-leaver is university-recommendation MEXT, after admission.

steps: In September 2026, build a spreadsheet of every English-taught programme you are interested in, with its intake month and its own deadline. There is no central portal and no shared calendar.
Decide April or September. For an IB student finishing in May 2027, September or October 2027 is the only realistic entry.
Ask your IB coordinator for predicted grades early — most Japanese applications are decided on predictions, an essay, a transcript and references.
Check whether each programme wants SAT/ACT or the EJU on top of the IB. If it does, book the test by autumn 2026.
Submit direct to each university through its own online portal, paying a separate application fee each time.

Do not build a MEXT application into the plan without checking first. If you hold Danish citizenship: the Embassy of Japan in Copenhagen offers Danish nationals only the Japanese Studies and Research Student types, both of which require you to be at university already, and ran no undergraduate call in 2026. Ask info@ch.mofa.go.jp directly. If you hold another citizenship, check the MEXT call of the Japanese embassy in your country of citizenship. The route that is open to a school-leaver is university-recommendation MEXT, which the university nominates you for after admitting you — so ask each admissions office whether it holds quota places.
Once you hold an offer, the university applies for your Certificate of Eligibility. You then take that to the Japanese embassy for the student visa. Allow three months.
application.selectionNotes: Selection is document-based and often interview-based rather than exam-based for English-taught programmes: transcript, predicted grades, personal statement, references and sometimes an online interview. This suits IB students who write well. The competitive bar at Kyoto, Waseda's Political Science and Economics, and Keio is high; APU, Akita and several regional programmes are more accessible.

Todai has raised its tuition above the national standard of 535,800 yen, which is the reason not to quote a national figure for any particular Japanese university.

The fee table linked from Japan's own official study-promotion site is drawn from the Student Guide to Japan 2019–2020 and converts at 114 yen to the dollar. It is the first thing an English-speaking applicant lands on and it should not be used for a 2027 or 2028 budget.

The structure to expect: national universities charge a one-off admission fee plus an annual tuition fee, both set nationally. Private universities (Waseda, Keio, Sophia, ICU, APU) charge considerably more and vary by faculty, with science and engineering highest.
Budget separately for the admission fee, which is charged once and is substantial, and for compulsory facility or lab fees at private universities.
Tokyo living costs are high; Beppu (APU), Akita and Sendai (Tohoku) are dramatically cheaper.

funding: MEXT (Monbukagakusho) Undergraduate Scholarship — nationally this is five years from April, one of them a preparatory year in Japanese, 117,000 yen a month, entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees waived, and an economy air ticket each way, with all classes in Japanese except where a grantee is directly placed at a university requiring none, and with MEXT rather than the student choosing the university. It is not open to you: the Embassy of Japan in Copenhagen lists only two MEXT types for Danish nationals, Japanese Studies and Research Student, and neither is this one. On a Danish passport, from a Danish gymnasium, treat the embassy track as closed until the embassy tells you otherwise in writing.

University-recommendation MEXT places — some universities nominate their own admitted students, and for a Danish national this is the only MEXT route that plausibly remains open, since it runs through the university rather than the embassy; other nationals may also have their own embassy's track. Ask each admissions office whether it holds MEXT quota places and how a new international entrant is considered for one.
JASSO Honors Scholarship — a monthly grant administered by the Japan Student Services Organization for privately financed international students. Check the current amount with JASSO.

Institutional awards decided at admission: Waseda states that recipients of its scholarships are determined by the admission result with no separate application, and that its awards are grants rather than loans.
APU operates tuition-reduction scholarships awarded at admission at several percentage levels — check the current levels with APU.
Kyoto iUP offers admission and tuition fee waivers plus monthly scholarships to eligible students.

funding.note: A full degree outside the EU/EEA follows separate rules, with its own ties-to-Denmark form: check su.dk before budgeting.

workRights: Students with College Student (留学) status may work up to 28 hours a week once they hold a blanket Permission to Engage in Activity Other Than That Permitted (Immigration Services Agency). Check the rules for longer hours in the official long vacations with your university.
residency: Non-visa-waiver process regardless of EU citizenship. The university applies for a Certificate of Eligibility on your behalf once you accept an offer; you then take it to the Embassy of Japan in Copenhagen for a Student visa. On arrival you receive a residence card and must register at the local municipal office within 14 days and enrol in National Health Insurance.
housing: Most English-taught programmes guarantee or strongly prioritise first-year places in a university dormitory or international house, which is by far the easiest route and usually cheaper than the private market. APU houses all first-year international students in AP House. Private renting in Japan involves key money, guarantor requirements and agency fees that are difficult to navigate from abroad — take the dormitory.
healthcare: Enrolment in Japan's National Health Insurance is compulsory for anyone staying more than three months and is arranged at the municipal office when you register. It covers roughly 70% of medical costs; students typically add the university's own supplementary cover. Your EHIC does not apply in Japan.

systems.name: MEXT Scholarship, Embassy Recommendation
systems.localName: 国費外国人留学生制度 (大使館推薦)

jurisdiction.authority: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), through the Japanese diplomatic mission in the applicant's country

coverage.includes: Undergraduate study at Japanese national universities, entered through a year of preparatory education in Japanese. Fields of study are chosen from MEXT's own table of courses and majors, with a first, second and third choice.
coverage.excludes: Art and music are excluded outright as majors. So, in practice, is the English-taught sector this destination is otherwise about: MEXT states that all classes are given in Japanese except where a grantee is directly placed at a university requiring no Japanese, and direct placement is MEXT's decision rather than the applicant's. The university is chosen by MEXT, not by the student, and no objection is allowed.

choiceRules.note: Three choices of major within one course, not three universities. Which university a grantee attends is decided by MEXT in consultation with the university and the preparatory institution, and a grantee may not transfer afterwards or change course.

systems.identityRequirement: None online. The application is made on paper to the Japanese embassy or consulate general in the country of the applicant's nationality, with a health certificate signed by a physician and a recommendation letter.
sharedSteps: Contact the Japanese diplomatic mission in your own country first. MEXT states that the process and the schedule differ by country and are the mission's to set, so the national page never carries the date you need.
Choose a field of study from MEXT's table — Social Sciences and Humanities A or B, or Natural Sciences A, B or C — and up to three majors inside it.
Sit the embassy's first screening, which includes a written examination and normally an interview.
Expect placement, not choice: MEXT decides the university.
systems.decisionModel: Two screenings. The Japanese diplomatic mission screens first, between May and August, and recommends candidates to MEXT. MEXT makes the second decision and allocates the university, taking account of the first-screening results, the applicant's achievement at the preparatory institution, the proposed major and the receiving capacity of each university and region.
systems.replyModel: There is no offer to weigh against another. A grantee who cannot arrive within the stated window, or who cannot enter a university after completing the preparatory year, loses the scholarship and returns home.

notes: Read from the 2027 undergraduate guidelines, published by MEXT in April 2026. The 2028 guidelines are expected around April 2027 and the terms may change; the allowance in particular is stated to be subject to the Japanese government's budget each fiscal year.

The Embassy of Japan in Denmark's Study in Japan page (read in a browser on 2026-09-24) lists only the Japanese Studies and Research Student types for Danish nationals, so this system has no Danish undergraduate dates to record. That holds for Danish citizens; other nationalities get dates from the Japanese mission in their own country. additionalGuidance.title: More about studying here
additionalGuidance.text: Japan's English-taught bachelor's degrees are a deliberate, named set built on top of the Japanese system, and the IB Diploma is one of the qualifications they were designed to receive. The University of Tokyo's PEAK closed after September 2026; its English-taught College of Design opens in September 2027 and names the IB first. Around it sit Waseda's six English-based schools, Keio's PEARL, Sophia, ICU, Kyoto's iUP, Tohoku's new Gateway College, APU and Akita. The Japanese year starts in April, so the September and October intakes exist mainly for international applicants — which is why they fit a May 2027 IB session, and why their deadlines run from October 2026 to April 2027, all before results.
